note: NGPC wildlife management area on the South Loup River north of Oconto. The campground (Google's 'Pressey Park') sits in a bend of the river west of NE 21, reached by about 1 km of gravel from the highway north of the bridge: a few designated electric sites at the entrance turnaround by the picnic shelter, then free primitive spots with tables and fire rings strung along the river road through the trees. Vault toilets, playground. A shooting range on the WMA can be noisy (camper reports). State park entry permit required. --Claude
summary: Still an NGPC WMA (state, agency-signed designated camping; NGPC Properties: Active, 1578.6 ac). NGPC's page is blocked, so everything rests on secondary sources: free (Broken Bow chamber), 14-night limit and FCFS (2023 camper review of the posted signs; campendium) -> fees and booking re-sourced as reported. PIN MOVE ~1.4 km: the stored pin is the south access by a pond; the campground is the river-bend area at 41.1912,-99.7152. WATERFRONT riverfront -> not waterfront (South Loup ~15-22 m wide = creek; sites under canopy). Electric 30 A and 35-ft limit stay unsourced.
flags: PIN MOVE: 41.1832,-99.7020 -> 41.1912,-99.7152 (elevation 740 -> 729 m), ~1.4 km. The stored pin (= campendium/The Dyrt points) is a gravel turnaround by a ~1-acre pond south of the county road, the WMA's south access; freecampsites' 2018 reviewer says the listed point is not the campground with the electric and calls the nearby 41.1825,-99.6970 the shooting-range lot. On imagery the developed campground is in a bend of the South Loup west of NE 21: gravel entrance road, turnaround with a picnic shelter, two small buildings (vault toilets) and play area, and NAIP shows two RVs parked at ~41.1910,-99.7157 and ~41.1915,-99.7149. Gravel tracks with pull-ins run on through the trees along the river. Google's 'Pressey Park' campground point (41.19358,-99.71040) is ~500 m NE on the access road in open grass. The reviewer's '41.1863088,-99.714729' is a hayfield across the river.

WATERFRONT riverfront -> not waterfront (down). The South Loup here measures ~15-22 m across on NAIP and Esri (under the ~30 m line, so a creek, not a river). The entrance sites at the turnaround are ~40-60 m from the water behind a tree belt. The primitive spots along the river road are under canopy; one bare clearing at the inner bank (~41.1915,-99.7143) may be a point bar. Imagery can only veto here, and there is no official site map or dated site photo. LEAD: creekside, if a photo shows the back primitive spots on the bank (The Dyrt, Aug 2023: 'almost all "primitive" camping spots are right along the water').

INCLUSION / OWNERSHIP state kept: agency-signed camping area ('Signs posted stated free camping for up to 14 days', 2023) with designated electric sites, tables, fire rings, vault toilets and a playground, a designated agency site rather than a parking-lot allowance, so not wma. No conveyance found (chamber and passport pages both call it a State WMA).

UNSOURCED (left as stored): hookups.electric 30 (no source gives the amperage; site counts conflict: '6 electrical hookups' in 2016, 'two spots with electricity' seen in 2023, 'A few designated spots' in 2021); sites.max_rig_ft 35 (only freecampsites' 2016 listing, user-edited); facilities.vault_toilets (2023 review: 'two outhouse style bathrooms', consistent). Water: freecampsites 2016-2017 mention a spigot / drinking water; not written.

FIT caveat: a recent Google reviewer (Timothy, ~Oct 2026) calls the spots 'lots of pull offs but short n tight'; a 2018 reviewer in a 22-ft truck camper would not return. Not a drop: the 2016 listing gives a 35-ft limit and RVs are visible on the entrance turnaround.

NOTE: 'reached by ~4 mi of gravel' was the south access; the campground is ~1 km of gravel off NE 21 (north access). 'max RV ~35 ft', FCFS/14-day and 'about 6 with 30-amp' removed as field-held or unsourced. 'State park entry permit required' kept but unverified: NGPC normally requires the park entry permit at parks and SRAs, not WMAs, and the page that would settle it is blocked.
